granularity: one learned node per complete device; terminal roles remain edge features
provenance_policy: Source availability and adaptations are explicit. These are controlled device-level adaptations, not claims of reproducing published benchmark scores.

preferred_repository_inspected.limitation: The inspected public revision does not publish its GAT, DeepGEN, GTN or MLP comparison implementations. Those models cannot honestly be labeled as extracted ZeroSim baseline code.

mlp.architecture: Canonical ordered device features, zero padding to max_devices, encoder_layers ReLU/dropout hidden layers of width ffn_dim, linear multi-metric output.
mlp.scope: Single-circuit fixed topology. No graph message passing, measured OP or OP missingness. The architecture is locally specified, not imported from an unpublished ZeroSim baseline.

xgboost.architecture: One independent reg:squarederror booster per observed performance metric; fixed canonical device parameter/mask/applicability vector.
xgboost.scope: Single-circuit fixed topology; package version, native booster, settings, selected rounds and feature order are saved by the runner.

gat.implementation: Dense native-PyTorch device adaptation of GATConv, mean-concatenation-disabled heads and ReLU; native mean-pooling linear graph-regression readout.
adaptations: Whole-device nodes and harmonized design-only features.
D/G/S/B terminal-pair channels add learned attention logits.
Configurable head/layer counts and attention dropout, batched dense masks instead of PyG sparse scatter.
No padding in graph pooling or attention keys.

deepgen_supervised.implementation: Dense GENConv channel-wise learnable-temperature softmax aggregation in preactivation res+ blocks, final LayerNorm/ReLU, learned-query graph attention pooling and MLP readout.
adaptations: Whole-device nodes, terminal-pair message embeddings, fixed-size padded dense batches, padding-aware BatchNorm in GEN MLP.

The native Node2GraphEmb readout retains 16 query chunks of width 16, three XAttn passes, and a 256-wide graph embedding. The query is registered as an optimized Parameter rather than the upstream buffer registration.

The graph-regression MLP retains BatchNorm/ReLU/dropout and uses encoder hidden width, while its depth follows decoder_layers instead of reusing encoder depth. Output expands from one scalar to the shared metric schema.

deepgen_op_pretrained.pretraining: Full selected continuous OP fields with observation/support masks on ID train only; real OP appears only in training targets. Then the pretrained encoder initializes supervised performance training with its native DeepGEN readout.
adaptations: The original circuit-fewshot work uses node-voltage supervision. This benchmark deliberately expands targets to the full supported device OP field set; it is not an exact original pretraining protocol.

zerosim_supervised.rationale: Uses the exact existing encoder and decoder family of the OP predictor and cascade models for the matched backbone comparison. See repository THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and docs/architecture.md for differences from ZeroSim.

accformer.implementation: Ported CR architecture: input linear embedding; pre-BatchNorm topology-masked multihead attention/residual/width-D ReLU FFN blocks; learned per-metric queries, cross-attention/residual/BatchNorm decoder and scalar output.
accformer.license_note: No license file was found in the inspected source tree. This user-specified repository is attributed explicitly; this document does not assign a new license to upstream code.
adaptations: Harmonized whole-device parameter/identity/port features replace CR's dataset-specific device feature vector.
Per-sample connectivity masks replace a single fixed netlist mask; terminal-pair attention bias retains D/G/S/B distinctions.
BatchNorm excludes padding and uses saved running statistics for a single valid training token.
Device padding is excluded from both encoder attention and decoder keys. Adapter graph token is removed before native decoder.
Shared configuration controls hidden width, heads, encoder depth and decoder depth; CR's internal FFN remains width D and is not replaced with the ZeroSim decoder.
